% Pictures sized by \includegraphics: width, scale, and height each give
% the picture the PDF's width, as a share of the text width, and a height
% never squashes it. tex4ht needs test-picture.xbb for a size it cannot take
% from the width alone. A picture without a size keeps tex4ht's size, and
% so does a picture that graphicx resizes in a box (a size after angle, or
% scale with a size), whose width is not the PDF's.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{graphicx}
\begin{document}
\includegraphics[alt={width}, width=100pt]{test-picture.png}

\includegraphics[alt={scale}, scale=1.5]{test-picture.png}

\includegraphics[alt={height}, height=96pt]{test-picture.png}

\includegraphics[alt={both}, width=100pt, height=40pt]{test-picture.png}

\includegraphics[alt={fitted}, width=100pt, height=40pt, keepaspectratio]{test-picture.png}

\includegraphics[alt={bare}]{test-picture.png}

\includegraphics[alt={rotated}, angle=90, width=100pt]{test-picture.png}

\includegraphics[alt={angle last}, width=100pt, angle=90]{test-picture.png}

\includegraphics[alt={scaled first}, scale=0.5, width=100pt]{test-picture.png}

\includegraphics[alt={scaled last}, width=100pt, scale=0.5]{test-picture.png}
\end{document}
